name: Relay
summary: Phone messages on your glasses, answered out loud.
description: A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives. Read it without taking the phone out, speak your answer, and it sends itself. Anything you miss waits for you in Messages.
author: Anezium

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives, and lights the display if it was dark. You read it where you are already looking, answer out loud, and the phone stays in your pocket.

## Reading

Each message keeps its sender beside it, so a group conversation reads as a conversation rather than a wall of text. A long thread turns pages instead of stopping at eight lines.

How long a message stays up normally scales with its length; *Message display time* in the plugin's settings holds every message for a fixed 5 to 45 seconds instead, for hands that want more time to reach the Reply chip.

## Answering

Speak your reply and it sends itself after a few seconds, counted down on the chip you are looking at — cancellable for its whole length, and never sent before you have seen what it heard. If the glasses went dark or lost the link, the clock stops and waits for you.

## Messages you missed

One you let go, or one that arrived while you were in another plugin, is in **Messages** in the Nexus menu: every conversation waiting on you, newest first, read and answered the same way. The list updates while you are looking at it.

## Hearing it instead

Turn on *Read notifications aloud* and the glasses speak the message as it arrives — the whole message, in the voice and at the speed you already chose in your Rokid assistant settings. It is produced on the glasses, so it works with the phone in your pocket and nothing leaves the device. Off by default.

## What it relays

Anything with a reply box, from any app. Nothing else, and nothing to tick first.

## What it keeps

Nothing. Messages live in memory while the plugin runs, are never written to disk, and never appear in a log. Revoke notification access and what it captured goes with it.

## Needs

Notification access on the phone, plus *Show on your glasses*, *Speech to text* and *Text to speech* in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access.

releases.notes:
- **After a reply is sent, the inbox comes back a bit sooner.** The "Sent" screen used to hand you back to the list after 1.2 seconds — which turned out to be the exact moment most people tap Back, so the tap landed on a list they had not seen yet and threw them out of Relay entirely. The hand-back now happens at 0.85 seconds: still enough to read "Sent", but the switch is over before your thumb gets there.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `6268b2f3867c956b9e16b8bfc5612ac3ed573faeafcd8820332bd5a78bd613fd`

- **Messages Android hides can now come through.** Since Android 15 the system blanks out any notification it reads as carrying a code — and it reads far more than real codes that way, so an ordinary message with a few digits in it arrived on the glasses as "Sensitive notification content hidden". The only exemption Android grants is to an app registered as a device's companion, which is exactly what Relay is, so a new **Show messages Android hides** entry under Access offers to register it with your glasses. It is off until you ask for it, and Android's own dialog tells you what registering covers before anything happens. The registration is worth having on its own: it also lets Relay keep running when the system would otherwise stop it, which is one of the ways a message used to go missing entirely.
- **When Android does hide a message, Relay now says so in its own words** instead of showing you the system's placeholder as though it were the message.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `bd73200282e03aaef4cd72e10758739539c53a0b08be153434add18c0abaf40d`

- **A message now waits for the glasses instead of being dropped after five seconds.** The link to the glasses drops and heals on its own all the time — a pocket, a doorway, standby — and healing routinely takes ten to thirty seconds. Relay used to give a captured message five seconds to reach the glasses and then silently gave up: the message sat in the inbox, and the band never came. A message now waits out the reconnection for up to two minutes and shows the moment the link is back. Relay also stopped trusting a "sent" that never left the phone, and transient hiccups during registration no longer throw the waiting message away. Pairs well with Rokid Nexus 1.2.8, which fixes a related blind spot on the glasses side for back-to-back messages.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `c378c901ae7aa9573effea3ef20776c0ddcc88e5fd3f9d6e95ed7fb2dcd100df`

- **Choose how long messages stay up.** Display time has always scaled with the length of the message, so a two-word text was gone in about four seconds — often before your hand reached the touchpad, let alone the Reply chip. A new *Message display time* stepper in the plugin's settings sets a fixed duration instead, from 5 to 45 seconds, applied to every message whatever its length. Auto, the default, keeps the scaling behavior unchanged.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `6196f4171745e929d6817f4f26cacb3148443b608850ab00a58d0cea0e197af0`

- **Read notifications aloud.** A new switch, off by default, has the glasses speak a message when it arrives — the newest message whole, not a preview. The band is held open while it reads and gives you the usual answering window once it stops. Answering interrupts the reading, and so does dictating. Needs Rokid Nexus 1.1.5; the speech is produced on the glasses, so nothing leaves the device.
- **"Sent" lands on the chip you were watching**, instead of confirming above a button still counting down to a send that already happened.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `8c380dd4610df0f6c6a4e35430fb96a7317768a57f460277820fec50655edf00`

- **Black out behind notifications.** A new switch, off by default, asks the glasses to hide everything else while a Relay notification is up — only the notification shows. Leaving it off keeps the band floating over whatever you were looking at. Needs Rokid Nexus 1.1.4; older hubs simply ignore the request.
- The test harness can crowd the inbox: an Eight threads button posts eight conversations at once, one more than the glasses list shows at a time.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `59104e1389207293374640f760476ca38faf5169dca8150ea6804a02cd9b4bf5`

- Relay has its own mark instead of the shared chat icon: two bubbles, the message that arrived and the answer going back. The same mark is now the app icon, so what you tap in the Store is what you find afterwards.

### Artifact

- File: `relay-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `95079f10de87ee4f7cd061cee51c24ad17c72f6724e50e99796f77528c2f4f03`

- First release: messages you can reply to reach the glasses as they arrive, and light the display if it was dark.
- Each message keeps its sender beside it, and a long conversation turns pages.
- Speak your reply and it sends itself after a few seconds, counted down where the answers are and cancellable for its whole length.
- Anything you missed waits in **Messages** in the Nexus menu, newest first, updating while you look at it.
- Nothing is stored: messages live in memory while the plugin runs and never reach disk or a log.
- Requires Rokid Nexus 1.1.0 or newer.
